notable_absence.finding: The umbrella page names no RBAC role for backup-service administration at all - not even a pointer to role:backup-admin, which the promoted registry already associates with Backup Service REST API access. Also notable: this page's SUBCOMMANDS list omits nodes-threads-map entirely (only settings, repository, and plan are listed), even though couchbase-cli-backup-service-nodes-threads-map.md exists as a sibling reference page in this same batch - an incomplete subcommand index, consistent with lighter TW review on this tree (a docs-issue-shaped gap: the umbrella page's own table of contents is stale relative to its sibling pages).

cross_component_finding: This is the central finding for this batch. Prior rounds established that cbbackupmgr (the standalone backup/restore binary) has NO plan object, no schedule, and no PRUNE subcommand - it only exposes direct one-shot subcommand invocations (backup, restore, merge, remove). This page confirms that finding is scoped correctly to cbbackupmgr specifically: it is couchbase-cli - a DIFFERENT tool, the general cluster-admin CLI - that exposes 'plan' as a first-class manageable object, via the backup-service-plan sub-subcommand ('[backup-service-plan](couchbase-cli-backup-service-plan.md)\n\nManage backup plans.'). So the correct statement is not 'no CLI has a plan concept' but 'the CLI that wraps the Backup Service REST API (couchbase-cli backup-service) has a plan object; the CLI that wraps cbbackupmgr's own archive-native operations does not.' This complicates rather than contradicts the prior finding: couchbase-cli backup-service plan/repository read as thin REST wrappers (see couchbase-cli-backup-service-plan.json for the JSON task schema, which matches backup:backup-task's BACKUP/MERGE task_type enum verbatim), while cbbackupmgr remains a wholly separate, plan-less, archive-native tool. Both CLIs are couchbase-cli's siblings/cousins in the corpus but operate on structurally different backends.
